purpose: SPEC-04 §2 addendum (2026-09-26) coverage + A1 conditions C8/C9/C10, FIX ROUND after opus review did not approve the first pass.

fixRound.note: This supersedes the round-1 evidence written earlier in this file (git sha ae42c88c6b7fc79941f2a6909e8615e226896cec). The opus review found tie-permutation.mjs invalid as an A1 C8 proof (it operated on abstract post lists, never the real page) plus 6 non-blocking issues. All are fixed below; nothing from round 1 is left unaddressed.
blockingFixed: tie-permutation.mjs rewritten: checkPageTiePermutation(url, kind, rawTextA, rawTextB, createdAtBySlug, topN) now extracts each side's OWN /blog/<slug> occurrence order directly from a real captured page body — an <a href> for '/', <url><loc> document order for /sitemap.xml (not lib/extract.mjs's sorted extractSitemap), a markdown list line for /llms.txt, a '### '-headed section (with a nearby 'Source: .../blog/<slug>' line) for /llms-full.txt — using ONE createdAt map built from A's /api/blog only. Runs the coarse group/multiset permutation check against that real order, then a residual check: reconstructs B's own text with its per-post blocks put back into A's exact slug order (every non-post byte of B stays exactly where B had it) and requires the result BYTE-IDENTICAL to A's own text, failing on any other difference. /blog is a fully client-rendered page (embeds /api/blog's own JSON as an RSC prop, no independently-diffable markup), so its residual check (checkBlogPageResidual) instead requires per-slug content-hash equality against A's/B's own captured /api/blog entries for the slugs the order check agreed on. The top-N boundary is now a RELATIVE test: B's shown slug SET may differ from A's only by members of the ONE tie group straddling the cutoff (never an absolute value comparison). lib/storage.ts's getPublishedBlogPosts() unconditionally prepends lib/arcAiArticle.ts's ARC_AI_ARTICLE_SLUG ('claude-commerce-agents-b2b') whenever the DB has no row for it — confirmed live (it currently sits first in /api/blog with an OLDER created_at, 2026-09-05, than the post right after it, which a real ORDER BY created_at DESC would never do); the checker detects that exact signature, requires the identical position on both sides, and excludes it from the rest of the analysis. The file header now states exactly what the tool proves.

Added self-test cases built from REAL captured data (docs/migration/evidence carries none of this raw data; it lives only in .scratch — see selftest results below): 'tie-permutation-real-data' runs checkPageTiePermutation/checkBlogPageResidual against the live captured raw bodies for /, /sitemap.xml, /llms.txt, /llms-full.txt and /blog — A-vs-A (self) passes for every one, and A-vs-(A + one extra text edit) fails for every one, with the residual check correctly attributing the failure to 'residual-content-difference' (or, for /blog, 'per-slug-content-mismatch').
nonBlockingFixed: tie-permutation.mjs: checkTiePermutation() now fails loudly (reason 'unpublished-item-present') on any published:false item instead of silently filtering it out; slug-set comparison is now a true multiset (Map of counts), not a Set+length check (which could hide e.g. A=[x,x,y] vs B=[x,y,y]); the CLI rejects a non-numeric/non-positive --top-n with an explicit FAIL and exit 2; every result carries tieGranularity:'millisecond' so a caller never mistakes calendar-day proximity for a tie.

urls.mjs source 1c (sitemap-b): fetchSitemapPaths() now takes an optional bypassSecret, sent ONLY as x-vercel-protection-bypass and ONLY to baseB's own sitemap.xml fetch (verified with a fake fetchImpl: A's sitemap/api-blog fetches never receive it, only B's does). buildInventory() now fetches 1b/1c's data early (still hard-fail-loudly) but defers the actual record() calls for 'blog-api-slug'/'sitemap-b' until AFTER every expect-bearing source (section 4's /api/admin/session /api/admin/posts, section 6's /blog?page=2), so a URL collision can never let a non-expect source silently shadow an expect block via push()'s first-write-wins dedupe. CLI gained --bypass-secret-file (read via readFile+trim, matching capture.mjs's own convention).

functional/run.mjs's checkCacheHit now also requires the second fetch to be status 200 with a non-empty decoded body, not just x-vercel-cache: HIT (a cached error page or empty body would otherwise still pass).

compare.mjs (A1 C10): checkBlogApiSize() (renamed from checkBlogApiSizeWarnings) now ALWAYS returns both sides' bytes/jsonArrayLength in the result (result.blogApiSize.sizes.{a,b}), not only when over threshold; the CLI logs them on every run. Threshold changed from 3.5*1024*1024 (3,670,016) to the exact 3,500,000 bytes the advisor text uses.

compare.mjs: the 'text' field's needsTextDiff handling now falls back to the raw .bin body in --raw-dir (via a new readRawTextPlainBody(), through the same normalizeText() capture.mjs applies) to build a REAL unified diff + classifyTextDiff when that side is compact and the raw file exists — verified with a live /robots.txt capture (mutating the compact side's stored textHash to a hash of an edited body and confirming compare.mjs's diff.preview is a real unified-diff string, not the {a,b} preview fallback). Falls back further to the short textPreview (or the other side's own available text) only when no raw file is available.

selftest.mjs: added 'mixed-mode-mutation-cases' — a field change (one /api/blog item's title) and a text edit (robots.txt), each run in BOTH directions (full-A vs compact-B, compact-A vs full-B) and each required to be DETECTED, not just that unmutated sides agree (which the existing 'mixed-mode-compare-both-directions' determinism-style check already covered). Added 'real-compact-capture-path': the REAL capture({compact:true}) code path exercised once live (2 URLs: /api/blog + /robots.txt — cheap), asserting the resulting manifest actually carries jsonBySlugHash/textHash (never the full-mode jsonBySlug/jsonCanonical/text fields).

changedFiles.change: Fix round: fetchSitemapPaths() takes an optional bypassSecret (x-vercel-protection-bypass only); buildInventory() takes baseBBypassSecret (sent only to baseB); 1b/1c's record() calls moved to after all expect-bearing sources (still fetched early, still hard-fail-loudly on error). CLI gained --bypass-secret-file. (Round 1 additions — sources 1b 'blog-api-slug' and 1c 'sitemap-b', both hard-failing on fetch error — are otherwise unchanged.)

Unchanged since round 1 (no review finding against it): --compact flag, buildCompactBlogArrayFields()/buildCompactTextFields(), compact /api/blog (jsonArrayLength+jsonBySlugHash+slugMultiset) and text/plain (textHash+textPreview) fields, full mode byte-identical to pre-update.

Fix round: checkBlogApiSize() always emits both sides' bytes/jsonArrayLength (not gated on the threshold); threshold changed to the exact 3,500,000 bytes; new readRawTextPlainBody() raw-body-through-normalizeText() fallback for the 'text' field when a side is compact, producing a real unified diff/classification instead of only a short preview when the raw file is available. (Round 1's mode-agnostic perSlugHash()/textHashOf() logic is otherwise unchanged.)

Rewritten (round 1's version worked on abstract post lists and was rejected as not a valid page-URL proof). New primary entry point checkPageTiePermutation() operates on real captured page bodies per URL kind (href/sitemap/llms-line/llms-section/blog-embedded-json), with a byte-identical residual reconstruction check and pinned-fallback-article handling (see the file header and the fixRound.blockingFixed entry above). checkTiePermutation() (the core algorithm) gained the multiset/published-item/millisecond-note fixes. checkBlogPageResidual() added for /blog. CLI usage changed to the new page-based invocation and rejects a non-numeric --top-n.
Fix round: checkCacheHit() also requires the second response to be status 200 with a non-empty body. (Round 1's --expect-cache-hit flag and opt-in behavior are otherwise unchanged.)

notScopedAsBulky.note: SPEC-04 addendum item 2 says 'other bulky fields (text, html) should become hashes as well'. Interpreted as: record.text (text/plain bodies, e.g. llms-full.txt) and /api/blog's whole-array/per-slug JSON (the actual multi-MB duplication C9 names). HTML pages already never store raw HTML or the extracted visibleText in the manifest (only visibleTextHash, plus moderate-size field/link/asset arrays) in EITHER mode, so there was no additional bulky HTML-derived manifest field left to compact without reducing per-field SEO/content diagnostic fidelity.
